mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3% in a quarter indicates a tightening labor market, which increases wage costs and boosts consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances when UNRATE decreases by more than 0.3% in a quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% in a month signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances when RSAFS increases by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% in a month signals increased economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances when INDPRO increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% in a month signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which reduces economic activity and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when HOUST decreases by more than 5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with high borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% in the same month, it signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200,000 and UNRATE decrease > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances when PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.2% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 2% in a quarter signals strong economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances when GDPC1 increases by more than 2% in a quarter.
